Dan Quayle was the forty-fourth Vice President of the United States, serving under George H. W. Bush from nineteen eighty-nine to nineteen ninety-three. He served during the end of the Cold War and the first Gulf War, representing the younger generation of Republican conservatives. Before becoming Vice President, Quayle served as a U.S. Senator from Indiana, having previously served in the House of Representatives. During his vice presidency, Quayle became the subject of mockery after misspelling "potato" as "potatoe" during a New Jersey spelling bee in nineteen ninety-two, a gaffe that defined his public image. He was criticized by the press and comedians throughout his tenure for apparent factual errors and verbal gaffes, including a confused reference to the fictional television program Murphy Brown. After leaving office, he lost the two thousand Republican primary race for president to George W. Bush, ending his hopes of ascending to the presidency. Despite the attempts, Quayle remained active in conservative politics and commentary, eventually becoming a major investor and advocate for venture capital in the tech industry. His vice presidency was often portrayed as a one-term affair, overshadowed by President Bush's own popularity and foreign policy focus.
